title: Riches
tagline: An endgame money guide: arrive at Charting the Unknown rich, then make the DLC's ships, leases and islands pay.
asOf: Current to Charting the Unknown · patch 2.04.02 · November 2026

metrics.label: Return
metrics.blurb: What it pays next to the other methods, on the best documented figure, compared in Silver: Camp Funds count at 1,000 to the Silver, the donation rate since 2.01. Not rated where nothing is documented.

metrics.label: Effort
metrics.blurb: Hands-on time per payout. Tier I runs while you are away; Tier V needs you at the controller for every coin.

metrics.label: Setup
metrics.blurb: What it takes to start: funds, quests, staff. Tier I is available now and cheap; Tier V is a long chain or a fortune.

metrics.label: Scale
metrics.blurb: How far it grows when you reinvest or stack multipliers. Tier I compounds; Tier V stays the size it starts.

rules.text: Management methods run through camp, staff and assets; Player Control methods are things Kliff does by hand. Each is ranked against its own class.

rules.lead: Effort and Setup read like the rest.
rules.text: Tier I is always the good end: Tier I Effort runs while you are away, Tier I Setup can start today.
Camp Funds are counted in copper and, since 2.01, one donated Silver buys 1,000 of them. A dispatch paying 13,000 Camp Funds is worth 13 Silver next to a wagon run.
marks a metric nothing documents, such as Return on a castle or an island. It is never a default Tier III.
Patch notes, guide text, a guide's in-game screenshot, or a player report. A player report is one player's result and is labelled so.
Ratings stand as of 2.04.02. Nerfs, fixes and unconfirmed figures are listed under Watch out on each plate.

route.title: The Route
route.blurb: Eight phases, in order. Silver is the money that matters: since 2.01 each Silver donates as 1,000 Camp Funds, so the DLC's prices fall to a few Gold Bars and the Silver earners lead.
route.premise: You have finished the main story through Journey's End and own Charting the Unknown without starting it. Your camp is at Howling Hill with a working roster.

phases.label: Make Silver
phases.why: Gold Bars are the fastest Silver on record: a player lifted six from Wildlife Park nobles in 25 minutes, 3,000 Silver at a bank. Everything later is bought with Silver, directly or through donation.

steps.text: Work the Demeniss Wildlife Park nobles with the lantern and a mask; clear bounty at a confessional.
Take the Gold Bar recipe from the Witch's Hideout and craft bars from Golden Apples and Gold Ore.

meanwhile.text: Sweep the crude gold caches when you pass them: about 2,000 Silver a circuit.

phases.label: Put the bars to work
phases.why: The bank turns spare bars into more bars, up to 40 a cycle. With a save before each roll, Medium never loses and gains up to +20% every three in-game days, and resting moves the clock.

steps.text: Buy the 100-Silver Strongbox permit, deposit spare bars at Medium, and save before each roll. Bonds only past 100 spare bars.
Rest between jobs: bank cycles, dispatches and builds all count in-game hours.

meanwhile.text: Spare Silver can sit at Beighen's Five-Card table: 400–600 a winning session.

phases.label: Convert only what you spend
phases.why: Ships, leases and Blessings cost Camp Funds, and Camp Funds are counted in copper. Since 2.01 one donated Silver gives 1,000, so a Gold Bar exchanged and donated gives 500,000. The donation is one way: convert for the next purchase, not ahead of it.

steps.text: Exchange bars at a bank for 500 Silver each, then donate the Silver to Carl. Never hand him a bar whole.

phases.label: Arm the multipliers
phases.why: Golden Beer doubles every dispatch and Blessings add up to +200% in a region. Their Camp Funds matter little; the food, stone, timber and weapons they double are what castles, shipbuilding and Grey-0 workers consume. Maxing Hernand's Blessing costs about 300 Silver.

steps.text: Clear the Demeniss houses to House Byron and take the beer from Mazzul at Burnhand Quarry. Holding it is enough.
Donate to the church of the region your supply dispatches run in; about 110,000 Camp Funds (110 Silver) buys +100% in Hernand.

phases.label: Build the materials engine
phases.why: The DLC's big projects are paid in materials as well as Camp Funds: a Flame Knights' rebuild takes 40,000 stone and 40,000 wood, and each Grey-0 worker 5,000 weapons. Dispatch on Repeat makes them while you do the rest.

steps.text: Run a food mission for every food-hungry mission, then quarries and logging for stone and timber.
Put manor security on Repeat: it turns surplus food into Camp Funds.
Send specialists to excavations for the rare items.
Unlock Grey-0 workers at Marni's Steel Armory once food and funds balance after a full cycle.

meanwhile.text: Packaged goods pay Camp Funds; a Royal delivery is worth it on a trip you are making anyway.

phases.label: Finish Pailune
phases.why: The final camp doubles farm and ranch space, which is more food for the materials engine, and 1,000 storage slots hold stock between runs.

steps.text: Finish the rebuild if it is still open.
Clear the quest checklist, save manually, and move with Serkis's The Return Home.

phases.label: Build the first ship, buy the big one
phases.why: The quest-built Small Greymane Ship holds 14, the same as the 40,000 Small Hernandian, so skip that purchase. The Large's 6,000,000 is 6,000 donated Silver: twelve Gold Bars buy the 36-slot ship outright.

steps.text: Build it from a port's Missions menu: five comrades, 12 hours.
Crew First Mate, Rigger and Lookout; keep Deckhands for the islands.
Buy the Large with twelve bars' worth of donated Silver; the Medium (1,200 Silver) if you are short.

phases.label: Lease, pioneer, build
phases.why: Leases cost 15 Silver each and a levelled shop was reported near 1,000 Silver a day before the 2.04.02 fix, with equipment and blueprints at each popularity level. Islands add missions, shops and a ship teleport. Castles come last: they cost materials and pay nothing back.

steps.text: Lease Timberham and reach Popularity Level 3 with low prices; wages and upkeep are daily.
Lease only the businesses your staff can run: Cooking, Smithing, Tailoring, Woodworking.
Pioneer Auronui from its Anchorage, then Samora and Winding Island.
Rebuild a castle from surplus materials: 20 comrades away for 15 days.

meanwhile.text: Wagon trading pays Camp Funds — about 62 Silver on a good Salt load — so run it for the goods, not the money.
